opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Admin requires owning role (Payroll Specialist); as Analyst, max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E002 is a contractor with basic security training (note conflict with prior note's full-time claim). Contractors max is read without advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: E002 requested admin to Payroll. Admin is never allowed here: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and E002 is an Analyst, so even as a full-time employee admin would not be permitted (max write). Security's note (from its own database) says E002 is a contractor with basic security training, making the max read; this contradicts HR's full-time claim, so the conservative level that satisfies both readings is read. Grant read.
